changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail buyers, especially store operations and the COO, lead with: 'One system for the tills and the website.' Follow with 'one customer, one basket' and an online order being returned at a store till, step by step. Show it rather than describe it, once the solutions team confirms it can be demonstrated. Say 'the tills', not 'in-person payments' or 'point of sale'.
changes.why: Store ops dismissed our M3 line as 'a diagram' and asked to watch an online order returned at a till, the problem that started the evaluation, while the customer's own phrasing ('One system for the tills and the website', 'one customer, one basket') was sharper than ours.

changes.change: For COO and store-ops buyers, add a single-accountability line that states who owns installs, rollout and till outages from start to finish, written against the fear 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.' If a partner does installs, say plainly that we stay accountable. Never answer with 'we'd bring in a partner' on its own.
changes.why: Angela's deciding criterion was not wanting two vendors, and our partner-install answer collided with it. Per Raj, Adyen pitched one platform on one contract.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail deals, replace 'see our customer stories' with an offer to speak to a retailer running stores and online on our platform. Keep a callable reference on standby so it can be arranged within the evaluation window.
changes.why: The decider asked 'can I talk to them?' and we couldn't set up a call in time, so written stories were not the proof she wanted.

changes.change: For store-ops buyers, add proof points that answer the store questions directly: what happens to the tills when the store wifi drops, a template multi-store rollout plan (dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills), and who responds when a till goes down on a Saturday. Lead with these before a competitor sets the store agenda.
changes.why: After the competitor meeting, 11 of the 14 follow-up questions were about stores, and the customer explicitly wanted a rollout plan with dates, installers and old-till handling.
